retention_corridor.name: Retention Corridor
retention_corridor.description: A synthesis shell, 3.3 m of it: five bays cut into one wall, each holding the SAME single pass of a point through space under a different regime of keeping. none is a bay built and empty. trace is the pass in the ink it was written with, where it went. lattice rules the bay with a field of pale nodes on the back wall and on the floor and admits the pass only at legal positions — a stair, not a diagonal. archive keeps nine passes at once, none dimmed by age. wax is the Wunderblock: a dark slab at the back, five impressions graded by age, and the clearing sheet caught half peeled, so the same strokes are naked on one side of the peel edge and glazed on the other. Every mark in all five bays is read from a single pass computed once at build time. Nothing here moves, nothing here is random, and the artifact has no per-frame code at all.
interactions: walk the row from none to wax
compare the same pass under five regimes of keeping
look under the peeled sheet at the fifth bay and notice the first bay looked the same
retention_corridor.capacity: SEE that the five values of `retention` are not a scale — keeping more is not recovering more, and the bay where a mark is most legible is not the bay where most of it is kept
retention_corridor.qfep_connection: F is the pass: one rule, evaluated once, identical in every bay, which is why the row is a comparison and not five drawings. E is the five records, and they are irreducible to each other — a lattice cannot be recovered from an archive and neither can be recovered from a clean surface, which is why the family needed a word for the choice at all. lambda is how much of what happened you are willing to let the room hold. The dark spot is the corridor's two ends: `none` and `wax` present the same clean surface, and every system that says 'cleared' is standing at one of them without saying which.
retention_corridor.relationships:
Synthesised out of the eleven artifacts that declare a `retention` axis. Every one of them was read — code, registry entry, note, still_note and declines — and each contributed something this corridor exhibits rather than describes.

[[mystic_writing_pad]] is the origin of the vocabulary and the reason `wax` is a value: Freud's Wunderblock (1925) via Derrida's 'Freud and the Scene of Writing' (1967), a red-framed magic slate whose surface clears while the wax underneath keeps the lot. Its registry says the thing this corridor is built to make checkable — that the pad 'lies the way every memory system lies: it shows a clean surface and keeps the wax'. Its ink, ghost, wax, sheet and frame colours are taken here character for character, and its construction (slab behind, translucent sheet in front, impressions between, graded warm by age) is the fifth bay's construction.

[[draw_dot]] wrote the record apparatus the family reuses — five builders, a gated apply_grid_config, dot-clouds rather than line strips 'because this artifact's own truth statement is that a curve is only ever a dense set of point samples'. Its curve is this corridor's `hand`, its phase literals (1.31, +0.83 per archived pass, +1.70 per wax impression) are used unchanged, and its rule that the record is APPEARANCE ONLY is why nothing here animates.

[[draw_dot_time_domain]] inherits the whole apparatus from draw_dot rather than restating it, and its promotion was a fix to the CHECKER, not to the artifact — the declaration gate now follows `extends "res://..."`. It also declined its own live trace as a subject, because with no player the draw sphere never moves and every sample lands on one point.

[[mario_cube_time_trace]] found that same decline independently, from the other end of the family, and its note says so. It is the one member that puts TIME ON A SPATIAL AXIS — its record is a waveform receding into +Z — which is where this corridor's `throw` comes from and why the bays have real depth and a ruling on the floor as well as the back wall.

[[player_trace]] is the family at room scale: a BODY writing rather than a hand, so its record 'lies on the ground plane rather than on a drawing plane' — 'the same five claims, same order, one storey down'. That is `walk`, which runs low across the bay floor.

[[grab_sphere_point_snap]] is the member that already had an opinion: snapping is the claim that a position must be LEGAL before it counts, and its promotion put that claim 'among four rivals rather than being the only thing on offer'. The third bay is its argument given a room, and the ruling is drawn at the quantum the code actually rounds to.

[[interactive_point_origin_force]] asks the sharpest form of the family question — 'does a reading survive the reader?' — because its mark is a measurement drawn while held and hidden the instant you let go. That is `reading`, a straight line, and its archive here is that artifact's own picture: past readings 'fanned to the same marker from seven past positions'.

[[oscillation_controlled_cube]], [[y_oscillation_cube]] and [[rotating_cube_demo]] are the driven-cycle members, and they are the two thirds of the family whose default is NOT `none` — y_oscillation_cube ships at `wax`, rotating_cube_demo at `trace`. Their mark returns to itself, which is `cycle`, and it is the movement that shows `archive` is not always destruction: nine phase-shifted copies of a periodic mark braid instead of blur.

[[draw_triangle_faces]] extends draw_dot and closes loops into surfaces; it declares the axis and inherits the apparatus, and it is counted in the census as a hand.

Structurally this is [[evidence_ladder]]'s rule: one phenomenon evaluated ONCE at build time and drawn N ways side by side, so that nothing on the bench can disagree with anything else on it because there is nothing else for it to agree with. It also takes that artifact's ruling about family words — see dna.kin. It replaces none of its sources: the walk-scale encounter with one artifact standing in one regime is the curriculum, and this is the room that wants the comparison.

dna.default:
movement=hand. A synthesis has no shipped placements, so the default is a free design choice, and this is the strongest single reading rather than the emptiest. The subject of this artifact is the CORRIDOR — the five regimes standing at once — so the pass underneath it should be the family's plainest and most common mark. Five of the eleven sources make exactly this mark (draw_dot, draw_dot_time_domain, draw_triangle_faces, grab_sphere_point_snap, mystic_writing_pad: a hand writing in a frame), and the curve drawn at this value is draw_dot's own _ret_curve rescaled, so the default bay-for-bay reproduces what the family's own record apparatus has always drawn. It is also the movement that makes the corridor's central finding hardest to miss, because a scribble is the mark `archive` destroys most completely.

NO PRESERVATION QUESTION ARISES, and that is worth saying plainly rather than leaving implied: this artifact did not exist before this pass and has zero placements, so there is no shipped behaviour for a default to preserve. The rule that outranks everything in doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md is about promotions of placed artifacts; here it has no work to do, and the design freedom it would otherwise forbid was used deliberately (see the ink and cadence constants, which are NOT the sources' numbers and say why).
dna.was: synthesized from the eleven artifacts that declare `retention` (measured, not assumed: a sweep of every registry file returns exactly 11 declaring entries). Nothing was promoted here — this artifact did not exist. It is the cross-member argument those promotions left in registry notes, built as a body.
dna.note:
THE ARGUMENT THE CORRIDOR MAKES, and no member can make it. Read left to right the row is monotone in how much is KEPT: nothing, one, one-if-legal, nine, five-under-a-lid. Read for what could be RECOVERED it turns twice. `lattice` keeps less than `trace` does, because it keeps only what was legal and rounds the rest away — the third bay looks like a fuller picture than the second and is a poorer one. And `archive` keeps the most of any bay and can be read the least: nine passes at full brightness with nothing dimmed by age is the same picture as no pass at all, for a mark that wandered. So legibility peaks at bay two and retention peaks at bay four, and they are not the same bay. That turn is why the word was hard enough to need five values, and it is invisible to any artifact that can only stand in one regime at a time — which is every one of the eleven.

THE SECOND FINDING IS AT THE TWO ENDS. `none` and `wax` both present a clean surface with no live mark on it. draw_dot's own doc block says of `none` that 'the frame is empty: at rest this artifact shows no mark', and of `wax` that 'the surface is clean; the record is underneath'. Those two sentences describe the same photograph. The corridor puts them a walk apart, at the first bay and the last, so that the distance between an honest erasure and a friendly one is a distance you cover on foot. That is the whole of Freud's essay laid out as a plan, and it is the reason the bay order runs none-first and wax-last rather than the other way.

THE THIRD FINDING IS WHAT THE AXIS IS FOR. Where the two peaks part company depends entirely on the movement. `reading` is a straight line and survives all five bays — nine straight measurements fanned to one marker are still countable, and quantised it becomes the cleanest picture of rounding in the corpus, a stair where a diagonal was. `cycle` is periodic, so nine phase-shifted copies braid rather than blur and `archive` fails to destroy it. `hand` and `walk` wander, and by the fourth bay they are mud. Total retention and total illegibility are the same picture only for a mark that wandered — which is a claim about archives, made by an object, and it is the only reason this axis exists.

ONE PASS, EVALUATED ONCE. _run() fills _pass0 from _sample() at build time and the trace bay, the lattice bay, archive's newest and wax's freshest impression all read that one array; the older passes are the same function at earlier phases, which is what 'nine throws' has always meant in this family. This is evidence_ladder's construction constraint rather than a quotation of it.
dna.kin:
`retention` IS REFUSED AS THIS ARTIFACT'S AXIS, on the record, and the refusal is the design. All eleven members use the word to stand in ONE regime and forgo the other four. On this shell all five are standing at once and that simultaneity IS the object, so an axis whose every value demolishes four fifths of the exhibit is not a variation of it. That is evidence_ladder's ruling on `evidence`, and it lands here with more force because there are five bays and not four. The word is EXHIBITED instead — it names the artifact, it names the bays, it is engraved on the plinth under each one — and what turns is the pass underneath it. Adding a sixth value to hold a default would have been worse: it takes a family's word and quietly changes its value list, which is the failure tools/check_dna_declarations.py exists to catch one level down.

THE ORDER AUDIT, since the corridor had to pick one. Measured across every registry file: 11 entries declare `retention`, and they use TWO orders. Ten declare [none, trace, lattice, archive, wax]. One — [[mystic_writing_pad]], the origin of the vocabulary — declares [wax, none, trace, lattice, archive]. The obvious explanation, that a member leads with its own default, is FALSE and the corpus falsifies it itself: [[y_oscillation_cube]] defaults to `wax` and [[rotating_cube_demo]] defaults to `trace`, and both still declare `none` first. So the real split is that the ORIGIN artifact leads with its answer and every ADOPTER leads with the argument, from keeping nothing to keeping everything. This corridor builds the adopters' order, ten to one, and for the argument's sake as well as the census's: the two clean surfaces have to land at the two ends.

AND THE ORDER MATTERS MORE THAN A STYLE POINT, because build_dna_gallery trims value lists from the TAIL. Under the dominant order the first value a truncated sweep drops is `wax` — the Wunderblock, the reason the word exists, and the only value that argues with the other four. Under mystic_writing_pad's order it drops `archive` instead. Ten of eleven members are therefore one cap away from a sweep that quietly omits Freud. This corridor is immune to that specific hazard, because all five bays are built at every value of its axis and none of them is a sweep position — which is one more reason the word belongs on an object like this one.

`movement` IS THIS ARTIFACT'S OWN WORD and no sibling declares it (checked). `mark` was the first candidate and is UNAVAILABLE: [[catalyst_target]] declares mark = none|bullseye|grid|nimbus and [[interactive_point_origin]] declares mark = bead|crosshair|cage|halo, both meaning how a point is decorated rather than what passed through. Taking a word without its answers is the dishonest half of a shared vocabulary, so a third meaning was not added to it.

THE VALUE LIST IS THE FAMILY'S OWN CENSUS, derived and not invented. All eleven members were read and each makes exactly one kind of mark: hand (5 — draw_dot, draw_dot_time_domain, draw_triangle_faces, grab_sphere_point_snap, mystic_writing_pad), cycle (3 — oscillation_controlled_cube, y_oscillation_cube, rotating_cube_demo), reading (1 — interactive_point_origin_force), throw (1 — mario_cube_time_trace), walk (1 — player_trace). 5 + 3 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 11. The list partitions the sources exactly; no mark kind is left out and none is added.

DECLARED ORDER: hand, reading, cycle, throw, walk. The default first, and the rest in DESCENDING separation from it, so that a truncated sweep keeps the frames furthest apart and the weakest pair is the first thing dropped rather than the last thing kept. `hand` and `walk` are the two wandering lines on this axis and the pair most at risk of photographing alike; they sit at opposite ends of the list on purpose. This is a different rule from the family's own (which orders by argument) and it is stated here because the audit above shows what an unexamined order costs.
dna.wax_note:
WHY THE FIFTH BAY NEEDED A DECISION RATHER THAN A TRANSLATION, and this is the synthesis's own contribution.

Every member builds `wax` shut: slab behind, faint graded strokes, translucent sheet in front. Photographed head on, that is `archive` with a lid — the sheet has no way to declare itself as a SURFACE and the impressions have no way to declare themselves as UNDERNEATH, so the still shows dim strokes behind haze and the two-layer claim has to be taken on trust. mystic_writing_pad solves it in TIME: _lift_sheet() runs every clear_interval in _process, sinks the current trace into the wax and wipes the surface. That is the family's central mechanism and it is exactly the class of evidence this bench cannot hold — the info_board fault, arrived at from the far end.

So the corridor freezes the clearing. The sheet is caught HALF PEELED: it covers the left of the bay and stops at a bright vertical edge whose lip curls off the plane, and the right of the bay is bare wax. The five impressions run the full width, so the SAME strokes are naked on one side of that edge and glazed on the other, continuous across it. That is the depth cue a shut pane cannot give — not 'there is something behind glass' but 'this glass is over that, and it is the same mark either way'.

MEASURED, NOT STYLED. The first build hinged a full-height sheet at the top and swung it open. A lid rotating about its top edge swings OUT as sheet_h·sin and rises only as sheet_h·(1−cos), so at any angle that lets you see under it the free edge stood 0.27 m forward — 0.125 m past the pilasters, out of the shell, and inflating the union AABB that every other bay is framed against. The peel costs 0.05 m of projection and shows both layers better.
declines: `retention` AS THIS ARTIFACT'S AXIS — refused, see dna.kin. It would bite enormously, because four fifths of the frame would change between values, and that is most of what is wrong with it: the corridor's entire claim is that the five regimes are standing at once and that the row turns round twice, which is invisible to any object that can only be one regime at a time. The large number it would produce would be a measurement of the exhibit being dismantled.

`retention` AS A SPOTLIGHT — one bay lit, four dimmed. Refused on evidence_ladder's second ground, which transfers without modification: dimming is MOUNTING. It changes how the exhibit is lit, not what it argues, and that is the one thing an axis is not allowed to do.

A TIME AXIS — the clear interval, the ghost persistence, the write speed, the fade duration. These are the knobs the members themselves declined one by one (mystic_writing_pad's critical_parameter is literally clear_interval × ghost_persistence; mario_cube_time_trace and draw_dot_time_domain each declined a rate and an interval as 'the info_board result verbatim'). A rate, a duration and a decay are invisible to one still. The corridor's answer is not to declare them but to FREEZE the one moment they were about, which is what the peeled sheet does.

A LIVE MARK — a hand, a body or a cube actually writing into the corridor while you watch. Declined for the reason two members already found independently and reported against their own interest: with no player nothing moves, every sample lands on the same point, and the record degenerates to a figure that is identical at every value. The corridor draws the STANDING record, which is the only part of this family a still was ever able to hold, and it says so rather than shipping a bay that is empty for a reason the photograph cannot show.

A SECOND AXIS ON THE RULING — the lattice bay's quantum, swept coarse to fine. It is real, it is still-visible, and it is declined because it would change ONE bay out of five, roughly a fifth of the ink and less than the critic's hottest-5% window is wide once the corridor is framed. A faint verdict there would be a fact about dilution rather than about quantisation. The honest way to show it is grab_sphere_point_snap itself, at walk scale, which already exists and already ships that argument.

INSTANCING THE SOURCE SCENES — one draw_dot, one mystic_writing_pad, one player_trace and so on, standing in the bays. Refused because the sources are live interactive machines with grab points, tag systems, unlock thresholds, audio players, _process loops and per-frame trail rebuilds; five of them in one scene would be five rooms in a trench coat, and their live traces would each be the degenerate figure declined above. What the corridor needs from them is their CLAIM and their NUMBERS, so the phase literals, the colours, the wax construction and the curve of `hand` are taken from the source files exactly, and nothing else is.
dna.still_note:
WHAT SHOULD BITE AND WHAT SHOULD NOT, said in advance so a thin number is read correctly rather than filed as inert.

BAY 1 (`none`) IS IDENTICAL AT EVERY VALUE by construction, and that is the design, not a fault — it is a bay with a back wall, a sill and a plate, holding nothing. It is a fifth of the row that cannot move, exactly as evidence_ladder's first pier is a quarter of its row that cannot move. The other four bays change completely: `hand` is a scribble that doubles back, `reading` a single straight bar to a marker, `cycle` a two-period sine at constant amplitude, `throw` an arc receding into the bay's depth, `walk` a low meander along the bay floor. So four fifths of the ink moves.

STRONGEST AND WEAKEST PAIRS, predicted from the geometry rather than guessed. Strongest: `reading` against anything — it is the only value whose beads fuse into one solid bar (12 mm centre to centre against a 34 mm bead) and the only one that adds a marker sphere to all four keeping bays. Weakest: `hand` against `walk`, because both are wandering lines; they are separated by the fact that walk runs LOW (y from −0.258 to −0.222, a 36 mm band on the bay floor) while hand fills the bay (y from −0.249 to +0.250), and they are placed at opposite ends of the declared list so a truncated sweep never grades that pair.

MEASURED FROM THE SOURCE, not from a capture — no Godot was run, the brief forbids a second instance, and the next sweep should falsify these. The constants were read back out of the .gd file by script rather than retyped. Mesh AABB 3.28 × 1.60 × 0.54, diagonal 3.689, radius 1.845. Arc length of the canonical pass inside one bay: cycle 1.98 m, hand 1.34 m, throw 0.95 m, walk 0.72 m, reading 0.50 m. Bead spacing at 42 samples: 6.5 / 9.6 / 4.6 / 3.5 / 2.4 px against a 6.7 px bead — so cycle is the only value with daylight between beads (under 3 px) and reading is the only one that fuses, which is the correct way round. MultiMesh instances 816 at the heaviest bay set, roughly 24 MeshInstance3D and 6 Label3D: no collision bodies anywhere, so nothing here goes near the watchdog.

THE CAPTURE AABB IS THE REAL BODY and no layers = 0 anchor is needed. The MultiMesh carries the marks, but the marks are inside the bays and the bays are inside a shell built entirely from MeshInstance3D boxes, so the mesh extent already bounds every instance. This was checked rather than assumed: with the guard clamps disabled the free-path extents of all five movements across all fourteen phases stay inside the bay interior, 0/588 samples out of bounds, and the snapped path is 0/42 because _rungs() derives the ruling from the same bounds the clamp uses.

NO TEXT MOVES WITH THE AXIS. Six Label3D in the whole artifact — five bay names on the plinth and one header — all non-billboard so LabelFramer treats them as text already lying on a body and adds no plate, and not one of them names the axis value. Every pixel that differs between hand, reading, cycle, throw and walk is a mark the pass made.

IF IT COMES BACK FAINT, check the framing before the design. The subject is 3.28 m wide and 0.54 m deep and the varying ink is four bays of 0.50 × 0.60 inside it; this is the wide-flat case the brief's table warns about, and dna.framing is set for it. If a sweep is run --staged, a 1.6 m floor-standing shell does not want a plinth under it and the pair AABB will grow; measure unstaged. The one thing that could genuinely dilute is the lattice bay's 144 ruling nodes at 4.7 px each — they are meant to read as a field, not as marks, and a critic hunting the hottest 5% will find the strokes, not the ruling.
dna.framing_note:
ARITHMETIC, NOT TASTE, and computed from constants read back out of the script. Mesh AABB 3.28 × 1.60 × 0.54, diagonal 3.689, radius 1.845. capture_config_sweep fits by diagonal — radius / tan(FOV/2) × PAD × framing, FOV 34, PAD 1.9 — which at framing 1.0 puts the camera 11.46 m out, where the visible frame is 7.01 m across, the shell projects to 43% of it and ONE BAY'S RECORD is about 6%: the dilution floor, exactly. At 0.55 the camera comes to 6.30 m and the frame to 3.855 m; at the sweep's yaw of 0.62 rad the shell projects to 2.98 m, or 77% of frame width and 42% of its height, so the subject is about 32% of frame — the same share evidence_ladder measured and reported as the healthiest in the synthesis wave. It also sets the scale everything else here was sized against: 197 px per metre, a 6.7 px bead and a 4.7 px ruling node.

If the header label crops at this fit, raise to 0.60 (181 px/m, 27% subject) rather than shrinking the shell — Label3D is not counted by the capture AABB, which is the hazard rotating_cube_demo's still_note flagged, and the header is the one node here that sits outside the mesh extent.
dna.fixture_note: NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED, and the absence is checkable rather than claimed: there is not one call to randf, randi or randomize in the file, and not one node lookup, timer or reference to the scene tree outside this artifact's own children. _ready is ungated and builds the whole corridor standalone, so nothing has to be supplied for the still. There is no _process and no _physics_process — the pass is computed once at build time and drawn — so a capture's settle time cannot photograph this artifact half way through anything, which is the failure mode the 0.35 s settle rule exists for.
dna.budget_note:
816 MultiMesh instances at the heaviest bay set (81 wall ruling nodes + 63 floor ruling nodes + 42 × 16 stroke beads across trace, lattice, nine archived passes and five wax impressions), about 24 MeshInstance3D of shell and slate, and 6 Label3D. No collision bodies and no static bodies at all — the marks are decorative multitude and are drawn as meshes without collision, per the brief. Well under the ~3200 element budget and nowhere near the 8000 static bodies that flirt with the watchdog.

THE MARKS ARE DOT CLOUDS AND NOT LINE STRIPS, which is a legibility decision and a fidelity one at the same time: a PRIMITIVE_LINE_STRIP comes back a hairline in a 760 px still (the documented way an axis reads as inert when it is not), and drawing a continuous line would also quietly retract this family's own truth statement, that a curve is nothing but a dense set of point samples.
